The Court made the following Oral Order

:
Heard Sri D. Kishore Kumar learned Counsel for the Writ Petitioner; Sri Arjun Chowdary, learned Government Pleader for Revenue, Stamps & Registration; Sri T. Yogesh, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of Sri M. Ramu, learned Standing Counsel for NHAI and Sri G. Divya Teja, Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition and Irrigation.
2. It is the case of the Writ Petitioner that the Respondent Officials have encroached into his land without initiating any Proceedings in accordance with law.

He would submit that, by virtue of Notification for acquiring land for National Highway (Bangalore-Chennai Greenfield Express Highway) an extent of Ac.1.36 cents belonging to the Writ Petitioner was acquired.

The Writ Petitioner, as on the date of acquisition, was in fact holding an extent of Ac.1.46 cents in Sy.No.153/1A. The Ac.0.10 cents of land in the same survey number remained un-acquired.
3.
However, the Official Respondents herein were under the assumption that the entire land belonging to the Writ Petitioner stood acquired and have started the expansion work.

Sri T. Yogesh,
learned Counsel appearing on behalf of Sri M. Ramu, learned Standing Counsel for NHAI would submit that on 21.01.2025, the Department of Revenue (Land Acquisition Branch) has handed over the possession of the subject land to the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).

As the work progressed, the mango trees which were lying in the extent of Ac.0.10 cents were also cut/uprooted by the Official Respondents, while the Writ Petitioner has already approached this Court assailing acquisition process by filing the Writ Petition in the year 2023.
My Predecessor, vide Order dated 31.08.2023, had admitted the Writ Petition with a direction to file Counter Affidavit.
Pleading are complete.
4. Since the land was only given on 21.01.2025, as the work had begun, the Writ Petitioner has made a mention before this Court for urgent listing of this matter.
The matter was listed on 22.01.2025.
Sri T. Yogesh, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of Sri M. Ramu, learned Standing Counsel for NHAI, sought time to obtain instructions as regards the cutting of the mango trees.

On 24.01.2025,
this Court having considered the broad spectrum of the facts, had issued certain directions.

Since C S Subramanyam Naidu vs Union Of India on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150673665/
2 the dispute between the Writ Petitioner and the Respondents has boiled-down to conduct survey to verify whether the Respondents have encroached into the un-acquired land of the Writ Petitioner,
this Court had ordered for fresh land survey to be conducted under the supervision of the Revenue Divisional Officer and in the presence of the Officials of the NHAI Officials.

sentences.text: 5. Sri T. Yogesh, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of Sri M. Ramu, learned Standing Counsel for NHAI would submit that, in compliance with the direction of this Court dated 24.01.2025, survey was conducted on 30.01.2025 under the supervision of the Revenue Divisional Officer and in the presence of the Officials of the NHAI.
The Tahsildar, after the conduct of survey, has submitted a Report on 01.02.2025.
From the Survey Report, it transpires that, due to the oversight, an extent of Ac.0.10 cents in Sy.No.153/1A was left out un-acquired.
This fact is fairly admitted by Sri T. Yogesh.

He would submit that the left out area is also essential for the Official Respondents to complete the Project and would take steps in accordance with law for acquiring the said extent of land, thereby,
duly compensating the Writ Petitioner in accordance with law for the loss of land and the vegetation therein.

The photographs presented by the learned Counsel for the Writ Petitioner would indicate that all the mango trees were cut in the un-acquired area due to misapprehension that the said land also stood acquired.

Since the Writ Petitioner is still the owner of the land and the mango trees present in it, needless to state that the Writ Petitioner would be entitled for appropriate compensation according to the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
6.

The Respondent Authorities shall proceed in accordance with law.
No Order as to Costs.
7.Interlocutory Applications, if any, stand closed in terms of this order.
